newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-WEEKEND MATCHES IN THE ITALIAN LEAGUE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-WEEKEND MATCHES IN THE ITALIAN LEAGUE.

text.p: Matches scheduled for this weekend in the Italian Serie A (kickoff times gmt, league positions in parentheses)

Mission impossible for Perugia coach Giovanni Galeone. Not only has Perugia President Luciano Gaucci vowed to remove him even if the side win 24-0 but he must face in-form Bologna without five players - Massimiliano Allegri, Federico Giunti, Salvatore Matrecano, all suspended, and Alberto Di Chiara and Marco Negri, both injured. Bologna to win, Galeone to get the sack.

Beaten 2-0 by Udinese last week, Fiorentina could do with a home win. Foreign trio of Argentine Gabriel Batistuta, Swede Kennet Andersson and Portugal's Rui Costa, allegedly much in demand in Britain, play against relegation battling Cagliari, led by Sandro Tovalieri and Roberto Muzzi in attack.

This one time championship decider takes on a "do or die" aspect for both sides in need of a good result. Liberian George Weah and Yugoslav Dejan Savicevic lead the Milan attack against a Parma side led by strikers Enrico Chiesa and Argentine Hernan Crespo.

Surprise packet Napoli have already knocked Lazio out of the Italian Cup and, with a full strength side, will fancy their chances of a repeat. Lazio rely on the attacking trident of Giuseppe Signori, Roberto Rambaudi and Pierluigi Casiraghi.

With the scalp of AC Milan already on their belt, Piacenza cannot lightly be dismissed. However, league leaders Juventus, despite a mid-week Italian Cup elimination by Internazionale, should be too strong with an attack which sees the return of Croat Alen Boksic and Alessandro Del Piero.

Following their last minute 4-3 defeat by Sampdoria last Sunday, Inter regained kudos with an Italian Cup semi-final qualification against Juventus in mid-week. Inter have a full strength, multi-national squad to chose from, while Reggiana's limited resources are further weakened by the suspension or injury enforcned absence of defenders, Filippo Galli, Angelo Gregucci and Belgian Georges Grun.

With only the suspended Francesco Totti missing, Roma should have too much power for relegation battlers Atalanta, led by the league's leading goalscorer Filippo Inzaghi, on the 10-goal mark. Precisely the sort of game, however, that inconsistent Roma could lose.

Perhaps the most entertaining game of the day between two in-form sides. Sampdoria will drop their unsettled French midfielder Christian Karembeu, still desperate for a move to Spain, while Vicenza welcome back Uruguyan Marcelo Otero but will be without suspended defender Gilberto D'Ignazio.

Udinese's Danish defender Thomas Helveg is suspended while German striker Oliver Bierhoff is still out through injury and the latter will be replaced again by Brazilian Amoroso, scorer of both goals against Fiorentina last week. Struggling Verona may again drop their Brazilian, Reinaldo, in favour of Filippo Maniero and Nicola Zanini in attack.
